title: [Chapitre] II. Réalisations topologiques des réseaux : notes manuscrites (06/06/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: Chapter II of a 1986 manuscript on topological realizations of 'réseaux'. The previous page decomposes S^n along a hypersurface C with collar C x ]-1,1[, the two 'rives' (banks) lying in the two 'feuilles' X_{A,C} and X_{B,C}. This page, dated 7 June, makes 'sides of a closed subset' and 'cutting X along A' intrinsic and sheaf-theoretic.

(1) For a space Z, Comp(Z) = Hom_cont(Z,{0,1}) = Gamma(Z, (F_2)_Z) is the Boolean algebra of clopen subsets of Z. It is contravariant in Z.

(2) For A closed in X, with U = X\A and i: U -> X the inclusion, define the 'banks' of A in X as Rives(A,X) = colim over neighbourhoods V of A of Comp(V\A) = colim_V Gamma(V, i_*(F_2)_U). So a bank is the germ along A of a clopen piece of the deleted neighbourhood V\A.

(3) NB1. If A has a tubular neighbourhood with boundary S_{A,X} (the sphere-bundle or link), the deleted tubes V\A are homotopic to S_{A,X} x ]0,1] and are cofinal. Hence Riv(A,X) = Comp(S_{A,X}).

(4) NB2. If X is paracompact, then for any sheaf F, Gamma(A, F|A) = colim_V F(V) (Godement). Applied to F = i_*F_2, this gives Riv(A,X) = Gamma(A, (i_*F_2)|A).

(5) 'Découpage of X along A'. Let Ã = Spec of the sheaf of Boolean rings (i_*F_2)|A over A, i.e. the relative Stone space. Its fibre over a in A is the Stone space of the stalk colim_{W ni a} Comp(W\A), the set of local branches or local sides of U at a. Gluing gives X̃ = U ⊔ Ã, the space cut along A, with boundary Ã. Stone duality gives Comp(Ã) = Gamma(A, i_*F_2|A).

(6) Next page. There is a canonical map Riv(A,X) -> Comp(Ã), so choosing a bank amounts to choosing a clopen piece of Ã. Riv is a Boolean (idempotent) F_2-algebra. A 'bivière' is a pair {rho, rho'} with rho + rho' = 1, i.e. a splitting Ã = Ã_1 ⊔ Ã_2. A 'locally disconnects' X if there is a non-trivial bivière.

Purpose: an intrinsic notion of the two sides of a separating hypersurface (two-sidedness). This lets one cut a space along the walls of a 'réseau' and reglue the 'feuilles', presumably for the topological realization of combinatorial networks or maps.
errors: NB1 tacitly needs the deleted tubular neighbourhoods to be cofinal among all neighbourhoods of A. For non-compact A one must allow tubes of variable radius; the statement is fine with that proviso.

The next page says the map Riv -> Comp(Ã) is injective and bijective only under some hypothesis ('X ponctuel?'). But by NB2 plus Stone duality for the proper map Ã -> A it is already bijective for X paracompact (Hausdorff). The hesitation in the manuscript seems unnecessary, or the hypothesis is misread.
Minor: Ã is defined as Spec of i_*(F_2)_U, but this must be restricted to A (or the whole construction X̃ = Spec over X taken). The notation is loose but the intent is clear.

ideas.what: Boolean algebra of clopens as Gamma of the constant sheaf F_2; banks of a closed subset as germs of clopen pieces of deleted neighbourhoods
ideas.modern_name: germs of components of the complement; local H^0 of the link; relative ends

ideas.what: Gamma(A, F|A) = colim F(V) for A closed in paracompact X
ideas.modern_name: tautness of closed subsets of paracompact spaces

ideas.what: Cutting X along A as the relative Stone spectrum of i_*F_2, giving boundary Ã whose fibres are the local branches of U at points of A
ideas.modern_name: topological analogue of normalization or geometric branches (EGA IV unibranch); cut-open space; relative Stone space of a sheaf of Boolean algebras
ideas.usually_credited_to: folklore; cutting surfaces along curves is classical; sheaf/Stone formulation not standardly credited

ideas.what: Bivière and local disconnection: a splitting rho + rho' = 1 in the Boolean algebra of banks
ideas.modern_name: two-sidedness / local separation; related to the local cohomology sheaf H^1_A(F_2) = i_*F_2 / F_2

missed.claim: Cutting along a closed subset is defined as Spec(i_*F_2), exactly parallel to EGA's normalization of X in U, whose fibres count geometric branches. This gives a uniform topological 'branch space' for arbitrary closed A, whose fibres are local ends. Together with the exact sequence 0 -> Gamma_A -> F_2 -> i_*F_2 -> H^1_A(F_2) -> 0, it ties local separation to local cohomology. The point-set constructions in the literature (prime ends, cut-open surfaces) are not usually phrased this way.
missed.quote: Considérons Ã = Spec(i_*(F_2 U)), puis (X̃, Ã) ... Comp(Ã) ≃ Γ(A, i_*(F_2 U))
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Gives a functorial, sheaf-theoretic cutting operation usable in o-minimal/tame topology, stratified spaces and combinatorial realizations of maps/dessins. It is a mild conceptual unification rather than a new theorem.

missed.claim: The programme of topologically realizing 'réseaux' by cutting and gluing along such intrinsically defined banks is only begun here.
missed.quote: le découpage de X suivant A
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Possibly relevant to 'topologie modérée' as envisaged in Esquisse d'un programme, but only as a sketch.

deep.surprise_reason: An elegant sheaf/Stone-duality formulation of the sides of a closed subset and of cutting along it. The underlying ideas (ends, local branches, two-sidedness, tautness) are classical, and nothing here is a substantive new result.
transcription_corrections: 'vig. immergé' is uncertain; context ('admet un voisinage tubulaire') suggests something like 'bien/régulièrement immergé'.
The definition is written 'Rives(A,X)' and later abbreviated 'Riv(A,X)'; these are the same object.
'Comp(Ã) ≃ Γ(A, i_*(F_2 U))' is written in the right margin at the bottom, not in the main line.
The crossed-out word after 'X.' at the top is uncertain ('Comptables' is doubtful).
